title: Sign-in and the other doorway screens wear the site's dark Stage room, not the light Commons

source.ref: Owner 2026-10-19, signing in on a local dev server: style the sign-in card with the dark theme.

detail: FILED AND CLOSED 2026-10-19. PREMISE RE-TESTED: /sign-in renders light because only signed-out visitors ever see it (a signed-in viewer is redirected) and lib/theme/mode.ts keeps every signed-out viewer light on purpose (no fq_acct cookie, so no .dark). That law stays. The site's own dark look is the Stage surface (data-surface="stage", which the marketing SiteShell wears), so AuthFrame now carries it: the whole doorway (sign-in, check your email, native open, global error) goes dark, not just the card, so the step from the dark website into the network stays one room. Stage does not re-declare the glass panel, so auth.css draws --fq-glass-panel from Stage's raised card, and the pastel magic-link pill takes ink text (the mega footer's rule). Field focus ring is the room's text-strong; check:tokens and check:contrast pass.

verify.cmd: node -e "const fs=require('fs');const f=fs.readFileSync('components/frequency/auth/auth-frame.tsx','utf8');const c=fs.readFileSync('app/themes/frequency/auth.css','utf8');const miss=[];if(!/<main[^>]*className=\"fqa\"[^>]*data-surface=\"stage\"/.test(f))miss.push('doorway is not on Stage');if(!/\.fqa\[data-surface=\"stage\"\]\{--fq-glass-panel:/.test(c))miss.push('Stage panel still the light Commons glass');if(!/\.fqa \.btn\.pa[^{]*\{color:var\(--fq-ink\)\}/.test(c))miss.push('pastel pill text not ink');if(miss.length){console.error('LIVE-1112: '+miss.join('; '));process.exit(1)}"
